summary: Israeli strikes in Gaza killed three terror operatives from Army of Islam, PIJ, and Hamas's Jabalia Battalion, which the IDF says were advancing attacks despite the ceasefire. In southern Lebanon, the Lebanese army reported five soldiers lightly wounded by an Israeli strike in Kafra while assisting locals, though the IDF denied involvement in a separate IED incident attributing it to Hezbollah. Meanwhile, British maritime authorities reported an explosion near a vessel in the Strait of Hormuz as Iran-Oman talks on the waterway's management reach final stages and the IRGC denies any reopening agreement.
key_points: IDF confirms three terror operatives killed in Gaza strikes: Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams (Army of Islam) and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman (PIJ) in Gaza City, and Ahmad Khudar (Hamas Jabalia Battalion commander) in northern Gaza, saying they were advancing attacks. (Source: @manniefabian/58913)

Lebanese army states five soldiers lightly injured by Israeli strike in Kafra while assisting locals; Lebanese media reports blast in Kounine from IDF demolition of Hezbollah infrastructure. (Source: @manniefabian/58910)

IDF denies responsibility for IED that wounded five Lebanese soldiers in Kafra, stating it was a Hezbollah IED outside the security zone where IDF forces were not present. (Source: @yediotnews25/133516)
British Maritime Trade Operations reports explosion near a ship in the southern shipping lane of the Strait of Hormuz. (Source: @asafroz/52208)

IRGC-linked Fars News denies any Strait of Hormuz reopening agreement, saying the strait remains blocked amid US hostile actions with passage only via IRGC Navy-designated routes. (Source: @shin_persian/8787)

Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi says Iran-Oman talks on Strait of Hormuz management are in final stages, though Iran rejected Oman's proposal for equal division of transit routes. (Source: @VahidOnline/77709)

Trump states planned large-scale attack on Iran paused at request of Iran and Middle East countries to allow immediate, full reopening of Strait of Hormuz and end to Iranian nuclear threat. (Source: @kianmeli1/90555)
TankerTrackers data shows average 7.5 million barrels/day of non-Iranian oil transited Strait of Hormuz over past 21 days despite IRGC announcement of full closure. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/78598)

points: IRGC-linked Fars News denies any agreement to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, asserting the waterway remains blocked due to US hostile actions and that transit is only permitted via IRGC Navy-designated routes, contradicting reports of a diplomatic breakthrough. (Source: @shin_persian/8787)

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi stated that negotiations with Oman on Strait of Hormuz management have reached final stages, though Iran previously rejected an Omani proposal for equal division of transit routes between the two countries. (Source: @VahidOnline/77709)

A senior Gulf official told the Wall Street Journal that the UAE is urging the Trump administration to escalate against Iran, including seizing control of the Strait of Hormuz and considering ground operations, arguing Iran will not compromise without increased pressure. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/6025)

TankerTrackers data indicates that despite the IRGC's announcement of a full closure 21 days ago, an average of 7.5 million barrels per day of non-Iranian oil has transited the strait, with 13 million barrels of tanker capacity entering the Persian Gulf in the last 24 hours. (Source: @rodast_omiddana/78598)

Former President Trump revealed that a planned large-scale attack on Iran, potentially the largest since World War II, was paused at the request of Iran and Middle Eastern countries to facilitate the immediate, full reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and end Iran's nuclear threat. (Source: @kianmeli1/90555)

Defense Minister Israel Katz announced on live television his intention to replace Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth with Personnel Directorate chief Maj. Gen. Dado Bar Kalifa, citing Bluth's appeal of a restraining order against a violent settler as contrary to his policy of protecting settlers. (Source: @manniefabian/58915)

Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir opposed the move, stating Bluth commands the Central Command professionally and with full trust, and that no command changes in key positions are planned during this sensitive period without proper procedures. (Source: @yediotnews25/133521)

The IDF conducted strikes in Gaza killing three terror operatives: Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams (Army of Islam) and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman (PIJ) in Gaza City, and Ahmad Khudar (Hamas Jabalia Battalion commander) in northern Gaza, claiming they were advancing attacks on Israeli troops. (Source: @manniefabian/58913)

In southern Lebanon, the Lebanese army reported five soldiers lightly wounded by an Israeli strike in Kafra while assisting locals, while Lebanese media reported a blast in Kounine from IDF demolition of Hezbollah infrastructure. (Source: @manniefabian/58910)

The IDF denied responsibility for an IED that wounded five Lebanese soldiers in Kafra, stating the device belonged to Hezbollah and detonated outside the security zone where no Israeli forces were present. (Source: @yediotnews25/133516)

An Israeli strike in Gaza City yesterday killed Alaa Imad Khamis Tarams, a member of the Army of Islam, and Hassan Ibrahim Shehadeh Qahman, a member of Palestinian Islamic Jihad, both identified by the IDF as advancing attacks on Israeli forces. (Source: @manniefabian/58913)

A separate strike last week in northern Gaza killed Ahmad Khudar, a commander in Hamas's Jabalia Battalion, according to the military, which said the operatives were eliminated to remove the threat they posed. (Source: @manniefabian/58913)
The IDF justified the strikes during the ceasefire by stating the three operatives were actively advancing attacks on Israeli troops in the Gaza Strip. (Source: @manniefabian/58913)

The Lebanese army reported five soldiers lightly injured by an Israeli strike in the town of Kafra while they were assisting local residents, with no immediate IDF comment on the incident. (Source: @manniefabian/58910)
Lebanese media reported an explosion in the town of Kounine, apparently resulting from IDF demolition work targeting Hezbollah infrastructure. (Source: @manniefabian/58910)

The IDF stated that an IED which wounded five Lebanese soldiers in Kafra was not Israeli but belonged to Hezbollah, and the incident occurred outside the security zone in an area where Israeli forces were not present. (Source: @yediotnews25/133516)

Southern Lebanese villages including Khiam, Kfar Shuba, Ali al-Taher, Majdal Zoun, Shama, Bayada, Nabatieh al-Fawqa, Kfar Reman, Kfar Tibnit, Hadatha, Taloussa, Taybeh, Mansouri, Yaroun, and Alman al-Qasir were subjected to Israeli sweeping operations, artillery shelling, controlled demolitions, house burnings, and IED explosions over the past day. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382641)

Lebanese army forces deployed to Jiyeh to reopen a road blocked by burning tires following a killing in Taalabaya, indicating internal tensions amid the border escalation. (Source: @rasedal3ado138e/382637)

The United Arab Emirates is reportedly pressing the Trump administration to escalate military pressure on Iran, including potential seizure of the Strait of Hormuz and ground operations, arguing Tehran will not negotiate seriously without stronger coercion. (Source: @Faytuks_Network/602
